s: King Josiah celebrates a great Passover in Jerusalem. After his death in battle the last kings of Judah sin, and Nebuchadnezzar burns the Temple and carries the people to Babylon.
Cyrus of Persia lets the Jews go home to rebuild the Temple and returns its sacred vessels. Their enemies write to King Artaxerxes, and the work is stopped.
At the court of King Darius, three young guards hold a contest to name the strongest thing in the world: the first says wine, the second the king.
Zerubbabel, the third guard, says women are stronger, but truth is strongest of all. He wins, and Darius lets him go and rebuild Jerusalem.
The list of the families who return with Zerubbabel. They rebuild the altar, keep the feasts and lay the foundation of the Temple amid shouts and weeping.
Encouraged by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah, the Jews resume building. The governor writes to Darius, who finds Cyrus's decree and confirms it.
The Temple is finished and dedicated with joy, and the returned exiles keep the Passover.
Ezra the priest and scribe comes from Babylon with more exiles and the king's gifts. He is grieved to find that many have married foreign wives, and he prays in sorrow.
The people send away their foreign wives. Ezra reads the book of the Law to all the people, and they rejoice and celebrate.
i: 3 Esdras (called 1 Esdras in Greek and Protestant Bibles, and “Second Ezra” in the Ethiopian Bible) retells the end of 2 Chronicles, the whole of Ezra and part of Nehemiah: Josiah’s great Passover, the fall of Jerusalem, the return from Babylon under Zerubbabel, the rebuilding of the Temple, and Ezra’s reading of the Law.

Most of it repeats what you have already read in the Bible, with the events in a slightly different order. Its one new story, in chapters 3 and 4, is the contest of the three young guards at the court of King Darius: each must name the strongest thing in the world. The first says wine, the second the king, and Zerubbabel says women, and above all truth. “Great is truth, and stronger than all things.” His prize is permission to rebuild Jerusalem.

Some early Fathers quoted it, but the Council of Trent did not count it among the 73 books, so the Church does not read it as Scripture. It is printed here because the 1609 Douay kept it in an appendix.
